taxi.fareNote: Most Georgetown taxis run on informal fixed zone fares negotiated before the ride rather than meters; agree the price upfront.

emergency.note: Fire: 913. Tourism hotline and Guyana Police Force Tourism Unit also available; response times can be slow outside central areas.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Caution in Tiger Bay, Albouystown and around Stabroek market; avoid walking at night

hood_desc: Seafront district with government buildings, embassies, and the city's top-end hotels along the sea wall; best for business travelers and those wanting security and comfort.

Leafy colonial-era residential area with wooden Demerara-style mansions turned into boutique heritage hotels; suits travelers wanting character, quiet streets, and easy access to the Botanical Gardens.
The historic commercial core near Stabroek Market with a mix of budget guesthouses and casino hotels; good for travelers on a budget who want to walk to markets, banks, and colonial landmarks.
Quiet, well-guarded middle-class suburb near the National Park and stadium with guesthouses and small hotels; suits longer-stay visitors, NGO workers, and those wanting a residential feel.
Coastal strip on the East Coast Demerara road near Ogle Airport, the hub for domestic flights into the interior; ideal for travelers connecting to Guyana's rainforest and Rupununi eco-lodges.

water.note: Avoid tap water; use bottled or filtered water instead.

sys.n: Minibus network (privately operated routes numbered by area)

transit.pay: Cash only in Guyanese dollars, paid directly to the driver or conductor on board; fares are small fixed amounts per zone. No contactless or card payment system exists. Exact change is helpful.
transit.hours: Minibuses run roughly 5:00am-11:00pm on main routes; limited/no service late at night, when taxis are the only practical option.
transit.note: There is no formal municipal transit authority; private minibuses (often called 'route buses') are the backbone of public transport.

Long-distance minibuses to Lethem and the Rupununi
ferry: Demerara Harbour Bridge crossing (toll bridge, not ferry, for vehicles)
Parika-Adventure/Essequibo speedboat and ferry services (regional, not city)

tip.r: Not culturally expected; rounding up or 5-10% for good service at hotels/restaurants is appreciated but not required.

places.name: Backyard Cafe

places.name: Oasis Cafe

food.name: Cook-up rice
food.desc: One-pot Saturday rice simmered in coconut milk with black-eye peas, meat, thyme and pepper; the everyday comfort food of the coast.

places.name: German's Restaurant

places.name: Shanta's Puri Shop

food.name: Garlic pork
food.desc: Pork cured for days in vinegar, garlic and thyme then fried crisp; a Portuguese-Guyanese Christmas tradition that appears year-round in Georgetown.

places.name: German's Restaurant

places.name: Bourda Market

places.name: Oasis Cafe

food.name: Mauby
food.desc: Bittersweet bark infusion spiced with cinnamon and anise, served ice cold; an acquired taste that Guyanese swear cools you down fastest.

landmarks: St. George's Cathedral
One of the tallest wooden buildings in the world, this soaring white Gothic Revival Anglican cathedral is Georgetown's most iconic architectural landmark.
Stabroek Market
This bustling 19th-century cast-iron market hall, topped by a distinctive clock tower, has been the chaotic, colorful commercial heart of Georgetown for over a century.
Guyana National Museum
Housing eclectic collections spanning natural history, colonial artifacts, and cultural heritage, this museum offers an accessible window into Guyana's diverse past.
Umana Yana
This large, cone-shaped thatched benab, built by Indigenous Wai-Wai craftsmen, is a striking cultural landmark symbolizing Guyana's Amerindian heritage in the capital.
1763 Monument
Also known as the Cuffy Monument, this powerful bronze sculpture commemorates the leader of Guyana's 1763 slave rebellion and stands as a proud symbol of resistance.
Georgetown Lighthouse
This red-and-white striped lighthouse on the Demerara riverbank has guided ships since the 1800s and remains a charming, photogenic waterfront landmark.
Promenade Gardens
A tranquil green escape in the city center featuring fountains, manicured lawns, and colonial-era charm, popular for relaxed walks away from Georgetown's bustle.
Parliament Building (Public Buildings)
This grand colonial-era building with its columned facade has housed Guyana's legislature since the 19th century and remains a stately symbol of the nation's governance.
Botanical Gardens
Sprawling tropical gardens with giant Victoria water lilies, royal palms, and resident manatees offer a lush, photogenic retreat just outside the city center.
City Hall
This ornate Victorian Gothic building, with its distinctive clock tower and gingerbread trim, is one of Georgetown's most photographed examples of colonial wooden architecture.

train.note: Guyana has no operating passenger railway - its colonial-era lines closed decades ago. Travel is by minibus, car or river/coastal ferry.

intl.to: Moleson Creek for Suriname (then the river ferry) & Lethem for Boa Vista, Brazil
intl.op: small private minibus and car operators — arranged at the Stabroek terminal, no online booking

bus.note: There is no single official long-distance bus company with online booking. Shared minibuses and cars run east to the Suriname border (Corriverton/Moleson Creek, then the ferry) and, under a 2024 Guyana-Brazil agreement, overland to Boa Vista, Brazil via Lethem - both operated by small private/informal carriers you arrange locally. Bring your passport.

intl.to: South Drain / Nieuw-Nickerie, Suriname (departs Moleson Creek, ~3-4h east of Georgetown)

ferry.note: The MV Canawaima crosses the Corentyne River from Moleson Creek to South Drain, Suriname; it does not leave from Georgetown itself. Tickets are sold through the government FerryPass.gy system. IMPORTANT: the service was suspended from 4 February 2026 for emergency repairs with no confirmed restart date - check locally before relying on it.

half.name: Santa Mission
half.blurb: Arawak Amerindian village on the Kamuni Creek, visited by boat and road for cultural demonstrations and rainforest walks.

half.name: Madewini & Splashmins
half.blurb: Riverside eco-resort in the interior with a swimming lake, waterfall, and trails through secondary rainforest.

full.name: Kaieteur Falls
full.blurb: The world's tallest single-drop waterfall, reached by a small-plane flight over unbroken rainforest and back in a day.
